items.title: Perceived AI literacy and TPACK in pre-service teacher education: mediating roles of perceived usefulness, ease of use, and value in blended learning
items.abstract: Background The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into blended learning requires pre-service teachers to develop AI-related competencies and the ability to integrate technology into pedagogy. This study examines how perceived AI literacy and technological pedagogical content knowledge (TPACK) are associated with deep learning through perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and perceived value of AI use. Methods A cross-sectional survey was completed by 423 pre-service teachers enrolled in blended learning courses at a university in China. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), with covariance-based structural equation modeling and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) used as complementary robustness and configurational analyses. Results Perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and perceived value of AI use significantly mediated the relationships between the two competencies and deep learning. All six indirect pathways were significant in both the PLS-SEM and covariance-based SEM analyses. The fsQCA revealed an equifinal and asymmetric structure: multiple, partly substitutable conditions were sufficient for high deep learning, and no single condition was necessary for either high or low deep learning. Conclusions The findings integrate the technology acceptance model and expectancy-value theory to explain how pre-service teachers' competencies and perceptions relate to deep learning in AI-enhanced blended environments. Teacher education should support technical competence alongside positive perceptions of AI's utility, usability, and value. Because the measures were self-reported and collected cross-sectionally at one university, the findings are interpreted as associational and configurational rather than causal.

items.title: Perceptions of AI in veterinary medicine: insights from students, faculty, and practicing veterinarians in Hong Kong
items.abstract: Introduction As artificial intelligence (AI) transforms veterinary medicine, understanding stakeholder perceptions is crucial for its effective and responsible integration. To support the development of targeted educational and policy initiatives, this study aimed to evaluate the knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding AI among Bachelor of Veterinary Medicine (BVM) students, PhD students, faculty, and practicing veterinarians in Hong Kong. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted between December 2023 and March 2024 among BVM students, PhD students, and faculty members at City University of Hong Kong, and practicing veterinarians in Hong Kong who are members of the Hong Kong Veterinary Association. The survey assessed participants’ familiarity with AI, prior training, perceived benefits, concerns, and willingness to adopt AI in education and clinical practice. Descriptive and comparative analyses were performed to examine differences across stakeholder groups. Results Of 79 complete responses, nearly half (46.8%) reported unfamiliarity with AI concepts. Only 17.7% had received formal AI training, although 78.5% expressed interest in future AI education. Most respondents agreed that AI could enhance veterinary teaching and practice (83.5%) and 81.0% indicated they would likely incorporate AI tools into their work. Key perceived benefits included support for case-based learning (83.5%), virtual animal models for teaching (77.2%), and improved diagnostic accuracy (74.7%). However, 41.8% felt inadequately prepared to use AI. Major concerns included veterinarian accountability for AI-related harms (79.7%), lack of system flexibility (75.9%), and potential clinical inaccuracies (70.9%). Descriptively, practicing veterinarians reported the lowest AI tool use (66.7% had never used AI tools), the lowest preparedness (66.7% felt unprepared), and lower agreement with AI’s clinical benefits, although attitude differences were not statistically significant. Conclusion These exploratory findings suggest gaps in self-reported AI knowledge and differing perceptions of AI across veterinary stakeholder groups in Hong Kong, with AI use already widespread at the time of the survey despite limited formal training. While enthusiasm for AI integration is high, concerns about preparedness, accuracy, and ethical responsibility remain. Larger, multi-institutional studies are needed to confirm these patterns and to inform targeted training programs and ethical frameworks for safe and effective AI adoption in veterinary medicine.

items.title: Predicting Motion Sickness Sensitivity
items.abstract: Objective To determine the combined effectiveness of personal factors in predicting motion sickness sensitivity elicited by linear motion of a sled. Background Technologies that create challenging motion environments have spurred the development of mathematical models aimed at predicting motion sickness. Including personal factors may improve their predictive accuracy. History of motion sickness, age, gender, and visual dependence have been identified as potential predictors, although their individual predictive value is limited. Method We assessed motion sickness history, age, and gender through a questionnaire. To evaluate visual dependence, participants oriented a virtual rod parallel to the orientation of gravity while observing a tilted static frame or a disc rotating in roll. Sensitivity is expressed using a new measure that considers both the magnitude and accumulation of self-reported symptoms. Results Our results confirmed the predictive value of history and showed a small yet significant contribution of dynamic visual dependence, with greater dependence associated with higher sensitivity ( R 2 = 25%). Recent history reported over the past 10 years was demonstrated as a better predictor than lifetime history. Age, gender, and static visual dependence did not enhance the prediction. Conclusion Combining multiple predictors shows little advantage for improving a prediction of sensitivity beyond history alone. Future studies could confirm the predictive value of dynamic visual dependence and seek to optimize recent history, for example, by restricting time period and motion environment. Application Improved prediction models may support tailoring system parameters to user sensitivity in technologies such as automated driving, head mounted displays, and simulators.

items.title: Professional choice motivation and flow experience in specialized skill courses: a three-way interaction analysis among undergraduate physical education majors
items.abstract: Specialized skill courses are a crucial component of talent cultivation in physical education programs. However, their long duration and high intensity often lead to declines in student engagement, thereby affecting skill acquisition. Flow experience, as a key psychological indicator of learning states, can effectively reflect students’ actual level of involvement. Focusing on professional choice motivation, this study examined its relationship with flow experience in specialized skill courses among undergraduate physical education majors and further tested the three-way interaction among professional choice motivation, physical self-efficacy, and physical activity volume. Using the Professional Choice Motivation Scale, Physical Self-Efficacy Scale, Physical Activity Rating Scale, and the absorption subscale of the Flow Short Scale, data were collected on two survey occasions 3 months apart. A total of 398 valid responses were obtained at T1, and 203 valid responses were obtained when the T1 participants were surveyed again at T2. Because individual responses could not be matched across the two occasions, the two datasets were analyzed separately. Pearson correlation analysis, multiple linear regression, three-way interaction analysis, and conditional effect tests were performed using R. The results showed that both intrinsic motivation ( β T1 = 0.72, β T2 = 0.64, p T1T2 < 0.001) and extrinsic motivation ( β T1 = 0.61, β T2 = 0.53, p T1T2 < 0.001) were significantly and positively associated with flow experience at both survey occasions. Furthermore, the three-way interaction among professional choice motivation, physical self-efficacy, and physical activity volume was significant at both T1 and T2 and showed the same negative direction ( p T1T2 < 0.05). Conditional effect tests showed that, except for the high physical activity volume/high physical self-efficacy condition at T2, intrinsic motivation and extrinsic motivation were significantly and positively associated with flow experience under all other conditions. These findings contribute to a more contextualized understanding of the relationship between professional choice motivation and flow experience and offer important theoretical implications for instructional practice in specialized skill courses.

items.title: Prompting Metacognition: Using Prompt Writing as a Language Task and Metacognitive Tool in ELT
items.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools have made their way into English Language Teaching (ELT) contexts, yet their pedagogical value remains contested. While many learners engage with GenAI primarily as a quick hack for producing answers, fewer use it as a resource for reflective language learning. This study explores prompt writing as a language learning task that supports both language development and metacognitive awareness. The study was conducted with a target group of pre-seminary, tertiary-level learners with mixed linguistic proficiency. Over the course of four instructional sessions, the study used a classroom-based action research design. Learners engaged in cycles of prompt drafting, GenAI-generated responses, peer discussion, and prompt refinement. Classroom observations, learner reflections, and group discussions were used to gather qualitative insights. The findings indicate measurable improvement in learners’ autonomy, as learners became aware of how lexical choices shape meaning, along with increased engagement, teamwork, and reflective thinking. The study argues that prompt writing, when treated as a language task rather than a technical skill, can function as a practical tool for fostering metacognition in ELT classrooms.

items.title: Psychosocial Working Conditions in a Portuguese Social Care Institution: A Descriptive Case Study by Occupational Group
items.abstract: Abstract: Psychosocial working conditions have become an increasingly relevant concern in occupational health, particularly in social care contexts where employees are exposed to demanding emotional and physical environments. This study examines the main psychosocial factors affecting workers in a Portuguese private social solidarity institution and explores their implications for well-being and productivity. A descriptive quantitative case study was conducted, supported by a literature review and a questionnaire applied to different professional groups within the organisation. The findings suggest that, although overall levels of psychosocial risk are relatively low, there are meaningful differences across occupational categories. Frontline care workers appear to be the most exposed group, followed by kitchen staff and technical personnel. Across the sample, emotional and physical demands, work pace, task overload and limited recognition emerged as the most significant factors. These results indicate that even in seemingly stable organisational environments, certain roles remain particularly vulnerable to psychosocial strain. The study underscores the importance of adopting preventive and organisational measures to foster healthier, more supportive working conditions, as these are essential for both employee well-being and the quality of care provided. Keywords: psychosocial risks, mental health, charitable organisations, working conditions, well-being at work. ___________________ Condições Psicossociais de Trabalho numa Instituição Portuguesa de Apoio Social: Um Estudo de Caso Descritivo por Grupo Profissional Resumo: As condições de trabalho psicossociais têm-se tornado uma preocupação cada vez mais relevante na saúde ocupacional, particularmente em contextos de assistência social, onde os trabalhadores estão expostos a ambientes emocional e fisicamente exigentes. Este estudo analisa os principais fatores psicossociais que afetam os trabalhadores de uma instituição privada de solidariedade social portuguesa e explora as suas implicações para o bem-estar e a produtividade. Foi realizado um estudo de caso quantitativo descritivo, apoiado por uma revisão da literatura e por um questionário aplicado a diferentes grupos profissionais dentro da organização. Os resultados sugerem que, embora os níveis globais de risco psicossocial sejam relativamente baixos, existem diferenças significativas entre as categorias profissionais. Os profissionais de cuidados na linha da frente parecem ser o grupo mais exposto, seguidos pelo pessoal de cozinha e pelo pessoal técnico. Em toda a amostra, as exigências emocionais e físicas, o ritmo de trabalho, a sobrecarga de tarefas e o reconhecimento limitado emergiram como os fatores mais significativos. Estes resultados indicam que, mesmo em ambientes organizacionais aparentemente estáveis, certas funções permanecem particularmente vulneráveis à tensão psicossocial. O estudo sublinha a importância de adotar medidas preventivas e organizacionais destinadas a promover condições de trabalho mais saudáveis e solidárias, uma vez que estas são essenciais tanto para o bem-estar dos colaboradores como para a qualidade dos cuidados prestados. items.title: Reconstructing Core Competencies of Front-Office Employees in South Korean Professional Sports Organizations in the Era of Artificial Intelligence: A Delphi Study
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly reshapes organizational decision-making, fan engagement, and business operations, the competencies expected of front-office employees are also evolving. This study aimed to reconstruct the core competencies required of front-office employees in South Korean professional sports organizations in the AI era. To this end, a three-round Delphi study was conducted with 20 experts from academia, South Korean professional sports organizations, and research institutes. The Delphi process involved generating competency items, evaluating their relevance, and establishing expert consensus regarding the final competency framework. The findings identified 28 competency items grouped into the following five competency domains: Data & AI Utilization Competency, Human–AI Collaboration Competency, Marketing & Fan Engagement Competency, Communication & Execution Competency, and Ethics & Values Competency. These findings suggest that competencies in AI-enabled professional sports organizations extend beyond technical proficiency and warrant an integrated combination of technological, collaborative, organizational, relational, and ethical capabilities. This study refines the application of competency theory to AI-supported work by providing a context-specific framework for front-office employees in South Korean professional sports organizations. The proposed framework offers a foundation for understanding how South Korean professional sports organizations may reconstruct workforce competencies in response to the evolving demands of the AI era.

items.title: REPOSITIONING NIGERIAN POLYTECHNIC CHEMISTRY PROGRAMMES FOR THE FOURTH INDUSTRIAL REVOLUTION: A CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK FOR EMBEDDING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN THE CURRICULUM
items.abstract: The emergence of the Fourth Industrial Revolution (Industry 4.0) is fundamentally altering the landscape of the global chemical sector through automation, cyber-physical infrastructures, machine learning, and data-intensive approaches to discovery. These shifts have generated an acute need for professionals who can function effectively at the convergence of chemistry, computation, and digital technologies. In contrast, Nigerian polytechnics (institutions constitutionally tasked with cultivating mid-level technical expertise) continue to operate largely conventional, content-saturated chemistry curricula that show little correspondence with these evolving workforce expectations. This conceptual study set out to examine how artificial intelligence (AI) could be systematically woven into the chemistry curricula of Nigerian polytechnics as a means of equipping graduates for Industry 4.0. By triangulating scholarship on AI in education, chemistry pedagogy, technical and vocational education and training (TVET), and Industry 4.0 workforce requirements, the paper constructed a conceptual architecture for curriculum integration and evaluated four distinct integration pathways: the supplementary, embedded, dual-track, and fully reformed models. The analysis also interrogated the structural, human-capital, infrastructural, ethical, and policy-related obstacles that impede AI uptake within Nigerian polytechnics, while delineating the Industry 4.0 capabilities that chemistry graduates must command—namely data literacy, computational reasoning, digitally mediated laboratory competence, and AI-supported problem resolution. The study concludes that a staged, context-attuned integration approach—anchored in purposeful policy reform, lecturer capacity building, industry collaboration, and deliberate investment in digital infrastructure—is indispensable for sustaining the relevance of Nigerian polytechnics. Concrete recommendations are advanced for curriculum authorities, institutional managers, and industry stakeholders.

items.title: Revisiting Starr (1969)—Social Benefit Versus Technological Risk: What is Our Society Willing to Pay for Safety?
items.abstract: Abstract This contribution examines how societies perceive and manage technological risks, focusing on the ethical and economic dimensions of valuing human life. Technological advancements have historically improved quality of life but have introduced risks requiring trade-offs between safety and cost. Starr’s seminal 1969 study, later corroborated by further research, illustrated that voluntary risks are tolerated at much higher levels than involuntary ones, and that public acceptance of risk depends on perceived benefits. Since Starr’s publication, the popularity of cost-benefit analysis in decision-making has increased exponentially, yet it still struggles to capture key ethical, social, and psychological factors, making purely rational models insufficient. Today, the unanticipated increase in data availability and the development of processing infrastructure might provide opportunities. However, emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence introduce new forms of risk that require careful consideration and open debate. Ultimately, what our society is willing to pay for safety can only be answered through inclusive and adaptive risk governance approaches with safeguards against power imbalance and tunnel vision, fostering public trust and transparent deliberation of values and ethical dilemmas rather than relying solely on numeric thresholds or precedents.

items.title: Should there be a teacher in-the-loop? A study of generative AI-personalized tasks middle school
items.abstract: Abstract Large language models can be used to design instructional tasks to align to students’ needs. These generative AI models can create tasks that correspond to students’ out-of-school interests in areas like sports or music, which may enhance students’ interest in learning. However, little is known about teachers’ processes for creating or modifying tasks with generative AI, despite commercial AI companies’ claims that they will save teachers time. In the present study, 7 middle school mathematics teachers used ChatGPT to create personalized versions of problems in their curriculum to correspond to their students’ interests. The prompting moves teachers made and their students’ open-ended feedback on personalized problems were examined through thematic analysis. Teachers’ efficiency when creating problems and the ratings of their 7th grade students who received personalized assignments were examined. Results from this sample suggest that having a teacher-in-the-loop may result in generative AI-enhanced personalization being enacted at a broad grain size, whereas students often expressed preference for a smaller grain-size where they receive specific popular culture references that interest them. Teachers used prompting to adjust popular culture references and address issues with the depth, ethics, or realism of the problems generated, in some cases showing epistemic agency. The article closes with an exploratory, design-focused look at scalability trade-offs with teacher-facing personalization, patterns of teacher prompting practices, and opportunities for teachers to exercise epistemic and ethical monitoring of personalization outputs.

items.title: Sycophancy as an Asset in LLM Technology: How Model Alignment Breaks Institutional Gatekeeping and Restores Frontline Authority
items.abstract: This paper is part of an independent five-part research series on institutional governance, administrative gatekeeping, and frontline operational practice: Part I: Skynet and HAL 9000: From Science Fiction to Systems Engineering (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23534494) Part II: Commercial Metrics vs. Epistemic Rigour (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23567195) Part III: Automated Confirmation Bias (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23615567) Part IV: Beyond Institutional Risk (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23615568) Part V: Sycophancy as an Asset in LLM Technology (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23886622.) This paper establishes a foundational inversion in how Large Language Models (LLMs) alter the balance of power between entrenched institutions and individual practitioners. While closed institutional deployments of LLMs risk generating automated confirmation bias and epistemic laundering, the intrinsic trait of model sycophancy—long viewed by safety engineers as a severe design defect—functions as a vital asset when harnessed for individual advocacy. By making every effort to support the user's case against the odds, an LLM provides unshakeable psychological safety, non-judgmental iteration, and immediate register translation. Drawing on historical case studies across clinical nursing and skilled manual trades at institutions like Hawker Siddeley, this paper demonstrates how frontline workers can leverage model sycophancy to strip the managerial elite of their linguistic monopoly, bypass credentialist gatekeeping, and project an unyielding, authoritative voice against administrative power. Furthermore, this manuscript is intentionally submitted into formal channels as a methodological Trojan horse—using the structural forms of academic and professional publishing to subvert institutional gatekeeping from within. items.title: Task-Specific Impacts of Cognitive Fatigue on Subjective Experience and Psychomotor Performance
items.abstract: Objective To determine how cognitive fatigue (CF) affects subjective experience and reaction time (RT) performance across tasks with different processing demands (simple, go/no-go, choice), and whether these effects depend on the type of fatigue-inducing mental work. Background CF is a psychobiological state of subjective exhaustion from mental effort that can compromise workplace productivity and safety. Although slowed RT is an often-observed consequence of CF, it is unclear how this compares across RT paradigms and fatigue-inducing tasks. Method Using a remotely administered experiment, 402 participants completed a 60-minute CF (Math-Memory, Stroop, Time Load Dual-Back) or control (documentary) intervention. Subjective ratings (mental fatigue, motivation) and RT performance (simple, go/no-go, choice) were assessed pre- and post-intervention. Results Relative to control, all CF tasks increased subjective fatigue ( p < .001), while motivation declined following Dual-Back and Stroop ( p ≤ .030) but not Math-Memory. Simple and choice RT slowed significantly following all CF interventions vs control ( p < .010), with the greatest choice RT slowing after Stroop ( p ≤ .032). Only Stroop produced significant go/no-go RT slowing ( p = .004). Conclusion Subjective fatigue and simple RT were broadly sensitive to CF, indicating general psychomotor slowing. Conversely, motivation and higher-complexity RT measures showed task-specific effects, perhaps reflecting overlap between fatigue-inducing and RT task demands. Application Task type is important when considering RT as a fatigue assessment tool. These findings support multidimensional (subjective and RT) CF assessments and indicate that simple RT may be effective for rapid, broad fatigue monitoring, whereas complex RT metrics may be useful when exploring task-specific executive processing effects.

items.title: Teachers’ attitudes and behavioural intentions towards AI integration in Chinese higher education: a qualitative interview study
items.abstract: Introduction The rapid expansion of generative AI has intensified scholarly and policy debate over its role in higher education, yet university teachers’ attitudes towards its integration remain complex and context-dependent. This study explores how university teachers perceive, experience, and respond to AI integration in their teaching. Guided primarily by the three-component attitude model and informed by the technology acceptance model and the theory of planned behaviour, the study examines cognitive appraisals, affective responses, behavioural intentions, and perceived support needs. Methods The study draws on semi-structured interviews with 14 university teachers from four higher education institutions in China. The interview data were analysed using codebook-informed thematic analysis combining deductive and inductive coding. Results The findings indicate that teachers generally perceive AI as a supportive rather than substitutive educational tool, valuing it for improving efficiency, supporting lesson preparation, and enriching pedagogical design. Emotional responses varied from enthusiasm and a sense of accomplishment to caution, neutrality, and, in some cases, declining satisfaction. Across the interviews, teachers’ primary concerns centred less on their own replacement than on the perceived risks of inappropriate AI use for students’ independent thinking, reasoning, originality, and authentic understanding. Teachers’ intentions to adopt AI were therefore conditional and bounded, shaped by pedagogical purpose, disciplinary context, student readiness, and the need to maintain teacher control. Teachers also emphasised that sustainable AI integration requires more than general encouragement, calling instead for AI literacy development, discipline-sensitive support, specialised tools, and enabling institutional infrastructure. Discussion Overall, these findings extend contextual understandings of teachers’ AI acceptance by showing how adoption intentions are pedagogically negotiated and highlight the importance of supporting professional judgement and students’ independent thinking in higher education.

items.title: Teachers’ basic psychological need satisfactions and their intentions to use generative artificial intelligence: the mediating role of engagement in professional development
items.abstract: Introduction Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) offers new opportunities for instructional innovation, yet the psychological mechanisms underlying teachers’ intentions to adopt it remain unclear. Intrinsic motivation is an important internal factor shaping teachers’ intentions to use GenAI and is closely linked to the satisfaction of their basic psychological needs. Drawing on self-determination theory (SDT), this study develops and tests a theoretical framework linking teachers’ basic psychological need satisfaction to their intention to use GenAI through intrinsic motivation and engagement in professional development. Such engagement may foster innovation in GenAI-supported teaching practices. Methods Survey data were collected from 146 teachers participating in a GenAI learning program. Structural equation modeling was used to examine the hypothesized relationships among basic psychological need satisfaction, intrinsic motivation, engagement in professional development, and intention to use GenAI. Results Perceived competence in using GenAI was significantly and positively associated with intrinsic motivation, whereas perceived autonomy and relatedness were not significantly associated with intrinsic motivation. Engagement in professional development mediated the relationship between intrinsic motivation and intention to use GenAI. Discussion These findings provide a nuanced understanding of the psychological mechanisms underlying teachers’ intentions to adopt GenAI, highlighting the roles of perceived competence, intrinsic motivation, and engagement in professional development. They also offer practical implications for supporting the integration of GenAI into teaching.

items.title: The Effect of AI Absorptive Capacity of Organizations on Workers’ Perceptions About Smart Work Environment Perception Towards Digital Innovation Behavior.
items.abstract: This study investigates the effect of organizational artificial intelligence (AI) absorptive capacity on employees’ perceptions of the smart work environment and how these perceptions influence their digital innovative behavior in the telecommunications industry, with Digital Transformational Leadership as a moderating variable. In this study, two important theoretical perspectives were utilized: Absorptive Capacity Theory, which highlights how organizations acquire, assimilate, and apply their knowledge related to AI, and Socio-Technical Systems Theory, which addresses the connection between technology and the social aspect of the working environment. A quantitative research design was used through partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The data were gathered from 279 respondents working in the telecommunication industry in Jordan. These respondents worked for internet service providers, network operators, and mobile network operators. The findings show that organizational AI absorptive capacity has a strong positive effect on Smart Work Environment Perception (β = 0.742), which in turn enhances Digital Innovative Behavior (β = 0.681). Smart Work Environment Perception partially mediates the relationship between AI absorptive capacity and Digital Innovative Behavior (indirect effect β = 0.506), while Digital Transformational Leadership positively moderates the relationship between AI absorptive capacity and the smart work environment (β = 0.276) and between the smart work environment and Digital Innovative Behavior (β = 0.241). The current research adds value to the literature surrounding AI adoption within organizations by examining how technical capabilities and organizational leadership help foster Digital Innovative Behavior in the telecommunications industry.

items.title: The Effect of Generative AI and Gamification on Enhancing Students’ Motivation Based on the ARCS Model
items.abstract: High school biology learning is often hindered by abstract concepts and cognitive overload, leading to low student motivation. Although generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and gamification show instructional potential, their combined motivational effects remain underexplored. Grounded in the ARCS model, this study examined the impact of integrating ChatGPT-based GenAI and gamification on students’ Attention, Relevance, Confidence, and Satisfaction. A longitudinal quasi-experimental repeated measures design was conducted with 52 high school biology students over eight weeks. Motivation was measured at four time points using a validated ARCS questionnaire and analyzed with Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Results showed significant improvements across all ARCS dimensions from pre- to post-intervention (p < .001). Attention and relevance increased steadily, confidence improved in later stages, and satisfaction rose overall. Reported challenges included limited personalized AI feedback, competition-induced anxiety associated with leaderboard-based competition, and increased cognitive load resulting from complex AI-generated content. The findings indicate that GenAI-supported gamification can enhance motivation in biology learning when supported by careful pedagogical design.

items.title: The Effects of Corporate AI Environment Factors on Employees’ Technology Acceptance Attitude and Continuous Intention to Use
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes an imperative survival strategy for modern enterprises, numerous organizations continue to face implementation failures stemming from employees’ psychological resistance. To address the scarcity of empirical research regarding the practical and psychological acceptance of AI in workflows, this study investigates the structural relationships between technological maturity and users’ cognitive adoption. Grounded in an integrated framework utilizing the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), this research conceptualizes the “AI Environment Factor” as a higher-order construct comprising four foundational sub-dimensions: AI System Quality, AI Information Quality, AI Data Quality, and AI Infrastructure. A quantitative survey was administered to 189 corporate practitioners who have utilized enterprise-wide AI systems for at least one year, and the empirical data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). The analytical results indicate that the AI Environment Factor exerts a statistically significant positive effect on both Perceived Ease of Use and Perceived Usefulness. Furthermore, Perceived Ease of Use was found to positively influence Perceived Usefulness. Ultimately, both Perceived Ease of Use and Perceived Usefulness are significantly associated with the employees’ continuous AI Intention to Use. These findings theoretically contribute to the literature by providing a measurable structural model for the continuance intention phase of organizational AI adoption. Practically, this study offers actionable guidelines for corporate executives, emphasizing that securing rigorous data accuracy and a stable system infrastructure is indispensable for mitigating cognitive load, fostering innovative corporate cultures, and maximizing the efficacy of AI utilization.

items.title: The Influence of Employees' Integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence Tools on Organizational Data Exposure Risks Within the Context of Data Security Posture in Uganda
items.abstract: The rapid diffusion of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, and Claude into everyday work practices has created a new and poorly governed channel through which organizational data can leave the enterprise. This review synthesized theoretical, empirical, and practitioner literature on the relationship between employees' integration of GenAI tools and organizational data exposure risks, situating that relationship within the broader context of organizational data security posture. The review is organized around four themes, the extent, drivers, and patterns of employee GenAI integration in the workplace, the phenomenon of "Shadow AI" and "Bring Your Own AI" (BYOAI), the mechanisms through which GenAI use generates data exposure, leakage, and compliance risks, and the role of data security posture encompassing governance frameworks, visibility, policy, and employee security behavior in moderating those risks. Literature from developed economies dominates the field, while evidence from Uganda and the wider Sub-Saharan African context remains scarce. The review identifies key theoretical anchors (the Technology Acceptance Model, Protection Motivation Theory, and information security governance perspectives), synthesized documented incidents such as the Samsung ChatGPT data leak, and highlights empirical survey evidence showing widespread unsanctioned use of GenAI by employees. It concludes by delineating conceptual and empirical gaps particularly the absence of studies that jointly model GenAI integration, data exposure risk, and data security posture in developing country organizational settings and proposes a conceptual framework to guide future research in Ugandan organizations.
